pictures.scene: James Tissot, The Ark of the Covenant — the high priest in his breastplate kneeling with his hands raised before the ark and its winged cover, inside the curtains of the tent, a Psalm of David, O LORD who may abide in Your tent
pictures.name: pd_tissot_tabernacle

pictures.scene: Caspar David Friedrich, The Cross in the Mountains — the crucifix standing on the rocky summit among the firs with the last rays of the sun coming up behind it, who may dwell on Your holy mountain, he who walks with integrity
pictures.name: pd_friedrich_cross_in_the_mountains

pictures.scene: Jean-Francois Millet, The Angelus — the field worker standing with her head bowed and her hands folded over the basket at her feet, the church spire small on the horizon behind her, and practices righteousness, who speaks the truth from his heart
pictures.name: pd_millet_the_angelus

pictures.scene: Domenico Fetti, The Good Samaritan — the traveller carrying the beaten man on his back to the waiting donkey, who has no slander on his tongue, who does no harm to his neighbor
pictures.name: pd_fetti_samaritan

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, The Return of the Prodigal Son — the father in the red cloak laying both hands on the shoulders of the ragged son kneeling at his knees, the elder brother standing by and watching, who casts no scorn on his friend, who despises the vile
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_the_return_of_the_prodigal_son

pictures.scene: Jacques-Louis David, The Oath of the Horatii — the father holding up the three swords while the sons stretch out their hands to swear on them, but honors those who fear the LORD, who does not revise a costly oath
pictures.name: pd_david_the_oath_of_the_horatii

pictures.scene: Quentin Metsys, The Moneylender and His Wife — the dealer in his black hat holding up the little scales over the gold and pearls spread on the table, his wife beside him turning the page of her painted book to watch him weigh, who lends his money without interest and refuses a bribe against the innocent
pictures.name: pd_metsys_the_moneylender_and_his_wife

pictures.scene: Karl Friedrich Schinkel, Gothic Church on a Rock by the Sea — the great cathedral standing dark on its wooded height with its spires and buttresses cut against the last light, the water lying still below it, he who does these things will never be shaken
pictures.name: pd_schinkel_gothic_church_on_a_rock_by_the_sea

lines.text: O LORD, who may abide in Your tent?
Who may dwell on Your holy mountain?
who speaks the truth from his heart,
who has no slander on his tongue,
who does no harm to his neighbor,
who casts no scorn on his friend,
but honors those who fear the LORD,
who does not revise a costly oath,
who lends his money without interest
and refuses a bribe against the innocent.
